response.answer: Failures rose in every category between the prior two weeks (Oct 4-17) and the last two weeks (Oct 18-31), with total failures going from 16,506 to 26,359 (+9,853). The biggest drivers were: issuer declines (+3,858, from 5,141 to 8,999, about 39% of the increase), risk declines (+2,357, from 1,532 to 3,889, a ~154% jump), customer drop-off (+2,312, from 6,596 to 8,908), and technical failures (+1,326, from 3,237 to 4,563). Issuer and risk declines together account for roughly 63% of the added failures, so they are the first places to investigate (e.g., specific issuers/BINs or a risk rule change). Caveat: this query counts only failures, not total attempts, so it shows where failures grew but can't confirm the success-rate drop itself or rule out that overall volume also increased.
